themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% surge—suggesting a coordinated poster campaign or enforcement breakdown in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
3,900% spike indicates sudden, concentrated activity rather than gradual degradation
No prior spike pattern suggests new campaign or sudden lapse in city enforcement
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: Walk major commercial corridors (Fulton, Nostrand, etc.) to document scope and type of illegal postings; photograph patterns
Source reporting: Contact Sanitation Dept and Council member's office to learn if enforcement was paused or redirected; check if other districts saw similar spikes

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber/Lyft/Via) surged to 53 this week compared to a baseline of 10.9 per week over 8 weeks—a 387% spike—suggesting a sudden increase in illegal pickups, blocking, or aggressive driving in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 53 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 12.78)
Second-highest spike in entire dataset indicates sudden, resident-visible problem
Likely tied to street-blocking, illegal pickups on residential streets, or surge pricing events
reporting_angles: Resident impact: Interview residents on heavily hit streets about blocking, noise, safety concerns; ask about specific times/locations complaints cluster
Regulatory angle: Ask NYC TLC if they've received unusual complaints from Bed-Stuy; check if any company recently changed pickup zones or incentivized drivers to work neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Standing Water & Flooding Risk
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints exploded to 3 this week from a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike—raising concerns about drainage failures, flooding, or sewage backups heading into heavy rain season in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 3 standing water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
Even small absolute numbers represent massive proportional spike, indicating sudden localized event(s)
Timing is critical given NYC's seasonal storm vulnerability; suggests drainage or sewer system issue
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Map locations of the 3 complaints via 311 request; visit sites to assess whether issue is resolved, ongoing, or tied to recent rain/construction
Infrastructure investigation: Contact DEP to ask if storm drains or sewers on those blocks have known issues; check recent excavations or repairs nearby

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 14 this week from a baseline of 3.0 per week over 8 weeks—a 367% increase—signaling a localized surge in open-air drug use, dealing, or related street activity in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 14 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.5)
Eighth-largest spike in dataset; reflects resident perception of open drug activity
Concurrent with encampment spike (15 complaints this week) suggests possible connection: unhoused individuals clustering in specific areas
reporting_angles: Community impact: Interview residents and business owners about where/when they see activity; assess whether there's a specific block or corridor; document health/safety risks
Policy angle: Contact NYPD and Community Board to ask if precinct has noticed activity increase; request data on narcotics arrests this month vs. prior months; ask about outreach coordination

themes_detail.label: Encampment Cluster Forming
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 15 this week from a baseline of 2.9 per week over 8 weeks—a 422% spike—suggesting unhoused individuals are clustering in a specific area or that a service site closure/policy change displaced people into Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 15 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.65)
Concurrent with drug activity spike (14 complaints) and animal abuse spike (12 last week) suggests interconnected street-level safety deterioration
Timing suggests external trigger (shelter closure, service cut, weather, or enforcement sweep elsewhere) rather than organic drift
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: Locate the encampments via 311 data; photograph conditions, interview unhoused residents about why they've moved to Bed-Stuy, what services they need

Systems angle: Call NYC Department of Social Services and outreach teams; ask if shelters closed, intake changed, or if they've documented displacement from other areas into this district; check if Community Board has raised issue
